description:
What if Bengaluru gets too hot to play outside? What happens when a city runs out of water? And why does fixing one problem sometimes create three new ones?

Through worldbuilding and futures thinking games, you will explore sustainability challenges specific to Bengaluru and imagine the futures you'd want to live in.

Along the way, you’ll practise observation, systems thinking, creative problem-solving and collaboration, learning to connect the dots and question the world around you.

⚠️⚠️⚠️

WARNING: Do not send this to your friends, if you don't want them asking 100 questions per second.

We are not responsible for the dinner table debates that follow. 😈

Workshop Facilitator: Shubh R Wadhwa, Founder and Editor of Befizuli Sawaal Magazine

I’m a creative educator. That’s code for, I use visual design to tell stories, make ideas easier to understand, and hopefully spark a little curiosity along the way. Over the years, I’ve had the opportunity to exhibit my work at the Lalit Kala Akademi, spend a brief minute teaching at Tapmi, Manipal, NID (National Institute of Design), and work alongside farming communities to help bring their stories to urban audiences. I tend to think of design not just as something that looks aesthetic, but also as a tool for social impact. Befizuli sawaal is an extension of that belief.

What's BEFIZULI SAWAAL MAG?

A visually appetizing magazine, that pushes you down rabbit holes about how the world works

name: Build With Intent
description:
**Build With Intent**

*An experience in designing a life that feels like yours.*

We're constantly building something- careers, relationships, routines, expectations, futures.

But when was the last time you stopped to ask whether the life you're building is the one you actually want?

**Build With Intent** is an intimate, hands-on experience that invites you to pause, reflect, and rethink what matters most.

Through guided reflection, meaningful conversations, and a playful dollhouse-building experience, you'll explore your values, question the expectations you've inherited, and create a miniature representation of the life you want to make room for.

No perfect answers. No pressure to have everything figured out.

Just 90 minutes to get curious about the life you're creating and leave with one meaningful step towards it.

**Because a life you love doesn't happen by accident. It's built with intent.**

**Takeaways**-

**1. Clarity on what truly matters**

A better understanding of your personal values, what makes life meaningful to you, and which areas deserve more attention.

**2. A new perspective on their ideal life**

The opportunity to explore possibilities without the constraints of conventional success, and visualise what a more intentional life could look and feel like.

**3.One meaningful step towards change**

Instead of leaving with an overwhelming list of goals, you identify one realistic action you can take in the next seven days.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Gender & Patriarchy Explained
description:
**About the event**

Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

**About the Lecture**

What is gender? And what is patriarchy?

Do these categories affect only women, or can they shape men as well? Or people that live beyond the binary? Or, society itself?

What is the relationship between gender and patriarchy? How do we understand power? Further, what IS feminism? Is it activism? Or is it theory?

Is it about thought, ideas and concepts? Is it about causes and explanations? About effects and solutions? Is it social theory, or not? If yes, what kind of social theory is it?

This lecture aims to debunk some myths about feminism. It aims to unpack some of the above questions; it aims to put forward languages and ways of thinking to analyse gender and patriarchy in our worlds. It aims to introduce feminism - as theory building, as knowledge production.

**About the Speaker**

Dr. Gita Chadha is professor at the School of Art & Sciences at Azim Premji University. In her teaching career of over three decades, she has taught at undergraduate colleges of Mumbai University and on the international programme of the University of London in Mumbai. She designed and taught a first-of-its-kind course in Feminist Science Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences in Mumbai. She has outlined innovative pedagogic initiatives for integrating science and social science teaching for CSCS, Bengaluru and for the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), Bengaluru.

A PhD in Sociology from the University of Mumbai, her thesis, “Gender, Scientific Intuition and Genius: A Feminist Perspective”, argued that intuition as an epistemic category is both marginalised and appropriated in the making of scientific knowledge.

Her research writings have been in the areas of science studies, sociological reimaginations of a feminist sociology and methodological debates in research. Gita has been the Chairperson of the University Women’s Development Cell of the University of Mumbai. She has developed frameworks for feminist archiving at the Research Centre for Women’s Studies, SNDT University, Mumbai, India and at the NCBS Archives in Bengaluru.

**Event Details**

📅 Sunday, 25 October

🕛 1 PM – 3 PM

📍 Maize & Malt, ITPL Main Road, Bangalore [4 mins from metro]

**Your ticket includes:**

• 1 complimentary freshly brewed beer or mocktail

• First-come, first-served seating

**About Pint of View**

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 14 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

name: The Shift: Helloween
description:
**THE SHIFT: HELLOWEEN**

An ode to Bollywood's darker side.

Halloween has a different kind of horror when Bollywood gets involved.

Forget the usual Halloween playbook. This year, The Shift pays homage to Bollywood and the horror films that gave us haunted havelis, sinister secrets, supernatural encounters, unforgettable villains, and stories that stayed with us long after the credits rolled.

On October 30, we're bringing that universe to life with a night that blends cinematic nostalgia, unapologetic music, and a little beautiful madness. This isn't Halloween as you know it. This is Helloween, the Bollywood way.

**BEHIND THE DECKS**

**DJ Jasmeet** — Known for high-energy sets and an instinct for reading the dance floor, DJ Jasmeet brings Bollywood favourites into the world of electronic and club sounds. Expect familiar hooks, unexpected switches, and a dance floor that doesn't stay still for long.

**Sa-Rang** — Bringing together Bollywood, Bollytech, and Amapiano, Sa-Rang adds another dimension to the night's sound. Expect the nostalgia of Bollywood meeting electronic rhythms and global dance-floor energy.

**BEHIND THE BAR**

**Bombay Daak** — A modern take on India's culture, Bombay Daak celebrates the spirit of neighborhood drinking spots through inventive cocktails, nostalgic influences, and food made to be enjoyed over another round. Expect a bar takeover with character, where what's in the glass is just as much a part of the experience as what's happening around you.

**THE NIGHT, IN NUMBERS**

*DRESS TO DISTRESS.* Bring your most twisted horror look. The best-dressed guest walks away with ₹10,000 in prize money. Make it count.

**IMPORTANT:** A Helloween costume is mandatory. No costume, no entry. No refunds will be issued.

*THE SHIFT: HELLOWEEN*

*October 30 | The Humming Tree, Bengaluru*

*An ode to Bollywood. A tribute to its horrors. A soundtrack for the beautifully unhinged.*

The Shift is an IP of Foreword Culture.

name: DIY Camera Obscura
description:
Build & Experiment with a Handmade Pinhole Camera

Long before lenses and megapixels, there was the *camera obscura*—a simple box, a pinhole, and the magic of light painting an image. In this workshop with artist **Stuti Bansal**, you’ll make your own camera obscura from scratch, explore the principles of analogue image-making, and develop unique photographs using light-sensitive paper.

**You’ll get to:**

- Build your own **working camera obscura**
- Learn the science & history behind the camera obscura
- Experiment with capturing and developing images
- Take home your handmade camera + prints you create

**Who is it for?**

Artists, photographers, makers, students, and anyone curious about analog photography and light-based art. No prior experience required.

name: Perspectives of OCD - A zine making workshop
description:
Conversations about OCD often revolve around pop-culture representation, which centres on cleanliness and being organised. This workshop invites us to look beyond the diagnosis and to recognise the strengths, resilience, and humanity of individuals whose lives are often reduced to a diagnosis. We’ll create a space for experiences that often go unseen and unheard.

Through guided discussions, creative reflection, and collaborative zine-making, participants will explore these perspectives while contributing to a collective publication that captures diverse viewpoints about this disorder.

We welcome people with lived experience of OCD, their caregivers, students, educators, healthcare professionals, researchers, members of civil society organisations, policymakers, and anyone interested in mental health and creating more compassionate conversations around addiction.

name: The Humming Tree x Indian Music Experience x Jodhpur RIFF present Killabeatmaker (Colombia)
description:
**About the Artist:**

KillaBeatmaker is a Medellín-based Colombian DJ, producer, singer-songwriter and audio engineer known for blending ancestral South American and Afro-Colombian sounds with electronic bass and global club rhythms. His live band expands this sound into a dynamic fusion of live percussion, Colombian flute, synthesizers, vocals and electronic production, bringing together traditional instrumentation and contemporary club music.

Joined by Guadalupe and Yulian, the live setup combines Colombian folk percussion and gaita with Akai-driven sequences, MPCs and synths, creating an immersive, rhythm-heavy performance rooted in Colombia while looking firmly toward the global dance floor.

**The Humming Tree:**

The Humming Tree - A grassroots performance venue in Bangalore, running from 2013 to 2019 and in the process becoming a cornerstone of Bangalore’s independent music, art, and cultural ecosystem.

Now, in 2026, The Humming Tree is back in a brand-new, purpose-designed space in Indiranagar. Built across 12,000 sq. ft., the venue features a 600+ capacity performance space, world-class sound and lighting systems, and a diverse F&B proposition. More than just a venue, it’s a hub for creativity, culture and collaboration.
